flour.line: Wheat flour: its gluten is what kneading builds.

salt.line: A pinch lifts every other taste; a fistful is all you taste.

starter.line: A sourdough starter kept alive at the hearth: wild yeast and lactic bacteria.

rice.line: Short-grain rice: wash it until the water runs almost clear.

egg.line: Egg: its yolk is what makes fresh pasta silky and gold.

sugar.line: Sugar: boiled with water it passes thread, ball and crack, each a stage you can read in cold water.

tealeaf.line: A tea leaf: green wants gentle water, black wants it boiling, and over-steeped any of them turns bitter.

kansui.line: Kansui: alkaline water. It makes noodles springy and yellow (the gluten tightens; the flour's flavones turn gold).

mint.line: Mint: menthol tricks the cold receptor (TRPM8), so it tastes cool without being cold.

honey.line: Honey: sweet is the body's "energy here".

butter.line: Butter: fat may be a sixth taste (oleogustus), the one a craving reaches for.

chilli.line: A chilli: capsaicin is pain, not taste (TRPV1). You sweat as if angry.

bitterleaf.line: A bitter leaf: about 25 receptors watch for bitter, the body's poison alarm.

onion.line: An onion: cut it and it makes the lachrymatory factor, the compound that brings tears.

vinegar.line: Vinegar: sour is the body's "this may have gone".

kombu.line: Kombu: kelp, its glutamate the first umami Ikeda named (1908). Never boil it.

miso.line: Miso: soybeans fermented with koji (Aspergillus oryzae). It adds body (kokumi).
